sources.title: Mariko Horii Lab
sources.text: Research Focus Our lab focuses on understanding the placenta affected pregnancy complications. We use pluripotent stem cells to model the placenta in disease and study the pathophysiology of pregnancy complications at the molecular and cellular level. We are currently studying a variety of diseases such as preeclampsia, complete hydatidiform mole, and Trisomy 21. Lab News & Highlights ​ https://blog.cirm.ca.gov/tag/mariko-horii/ Maddie got into grad school and will be joining University of Virginia Summer of 2022. Congrats Maddie! Tony got into Master's program and will be joining Cal Poly SLO Summer of 2023. Congrats Tony! Contact Us We are located at the Sanford Consortium for Regenerative Medicine. Contact Dr. Horii if you are interested in the lab: Mariko Horii mhorii@health.ucsd.edu

sources.title: About
sources.text: About the Lab Location We are located at the Sanford Consortium for Regenerative Medicine. Please contact Dr. Horii ( mhorii@health.ucsd.edu ) if you are interested in the lab. Principal Investigator Dr. Mariko Horii Dr. Mariko Horii received her M.D. degrees from Kagawa University School of Medicine (Kagawa, Japan). Subsequently, she did her residency training in Obstetrics and Gynecology at St. Luke's International Hospital (Tokyo, Japan), where she was chief resident in her final year of her training. Following the clinical training, she joined Dr. Parast's lab at UC San Diego as a postdoc where she was trained in stem cell research. She has been funded by California Institute for Regenerative Medicine (CIRM) training grant and National Institutes of Health (NIH)/National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD) K99/R00. She started her independent research program at UC San Diego in 2020. Lab Manager Tony Bui Mr. Tony Bui has been working with Dr. Horii since 2016, when he was an undergraduate student at San Diego State University. He became a lab manager in 2020. He has extensive training in reprogramming, human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC) culture, derivation of trophoblast stem cells using hPSC, immunostaining (including the use of imageJ), and RNA. He also enjoys mentoring students in the lab, helping them gain experience in everything from the basic molecular techniques to advanced hPSC cell culture.
